questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To pick a country / city that is as different as possible to Denmark so I get to experience new culture, social life, learning and school system.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the time of my life. Amazing people, interesting course and fantastic city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was missing some information, but the professors and university staff is very open to help. I just send out mails to the different professors and other relevant staff - they respond very fast and helped me out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was assistance from the Erasmus coordinator and from the volunteering Erasmus Network.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Luckily it was easy to me, since I found my place to live trough connections.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus is amazing and you don't feel left out from the people living at campus - but pay attention to the area of the city you live in and the transport to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not offerende any housing available to students, so I can't speak about this.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a formular about the course you want to take at the institution and that's basically it. Following you need to make sure you have access to all the relevant online platforms used (contact the professors directly).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Official Erasmus coordinator was able to help with any relevant problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the Classes I wanted without problem - even if all the classes was master and im still doing my bachelor.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patient and relax - even if the system seems to simple and a little outdated it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the level was varying a bit. Some classes was more difficult and some a little easier - also depending on how much background knowledge I had that was relevant for the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Very long lectures and a lot of knowledge you just need to remember. Lab was nice since you actually got to do a lot of stuff on your own, but there was still assistance to help you if you felt lost.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ADVANCED MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY
BIOINFORMATICS AND MOLECULAR MODELING
PHARMACOGENOMICS, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, ORPHAN DRUGS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advanced molecular biology was a great course - I loved the teaching and we also got to spend time in lab. The work burden is a little big since there is also presentations and homework, but I really learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You go out a lot, so even if food and drinks are cheap you spend a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, living and drinks is less expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't do so many activities with the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus network is great for arranging events and meeting people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and student environment with local people - and travel as much as possible. I wish that I had spend more time going to cities nearby and on weekend getaways.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy since the Italians are such openminded and social people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are not all the best with English - if you can learn basic italian before going or have patience when speaking with them. And don't get offended if they don't want to speak to you - its probably just because they are shy and embarrassed about their English and not about you personally.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The dinner time was too late - they eat dinner at 22/23 and im used to eat 18/19.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the social and open culture. I love the Aperitivo culture as well - they fact that you can go out for one drink / beer and it doesn't have to be more than this - and you get to socialize.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn a little italian if possible - there are still a lot of young people not speaking English, so this could help you socialize easier with the locals. 
Take advantage of all the possible social events you find interesting - They are so good at creating events (especially Erasmus) and this way you not only meet other exchange students, but also local italiens who volunteer in the network. 
Travel and experience as much as possible - there are so many great options.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendship both locals and internationals, the language improvement by being forced to du presentations and exams in English and the culture - I really like everything about Milan.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I found it challenging to settle down and meet people - but it changes fast, as soon as you get in to a rhythm with lectures and social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
